title: A closed normalization point lifts to a completed branch
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means having a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and domain means $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ be its field of fractions and $B\subset K$ its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a prime ideal with $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m$. Put $H=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}A/\mathfrak m^n$, with canonical map $\iota:A\to H$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $\mathfrak n=\ker(H\to A/\mathfrak m)$, where the map takes a compatible sequence to its first component. There exist a minimal prime $\mathfrak p\subset H$, an $A$-algebra homomorphism $j:B\to T$, and a prime ideal $M\subset T$, where $T$ is the integral closure of the domain $H/\mathfrak p$ in $\operatorname{Frac}(H/\mathfrak p)$, such that $j^{-1}(M)=\mathfrak q$ and the contraction of $M$ to $H/\mathfrak p$ is $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak p$. Here $j$ being an $A$-algebra homomorphism means that its restriction to $A$ is $A\xrightarrow{\iota}H\to H/\mathfrak p\hookrightarrow T$. A minimal prime is a prime minimal among all prime ideals; fractions always have nonzero denominators.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules, Lemma 4.8.3, printed p. 84 (PDF p. 98), together with Corollary 2.1.13: component form of the normalization of the reduced completion. Author-hosted text read at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], $A\to H$ is faithfully flat, hence flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $H$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $H$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mH$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], list its distinct minimal primes as $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_r$. This list is nonempty: the prime $\mathfrak n$ contains a minimal prime by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime].

Put $C=H\otimes_A B$, with maps $h\mapsto h\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. The map $B\to C$ is faithfully flat directly from [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]: for any complex of $B$-modules $N_1\to N_2\to N_3$, the identifications $C\otimes_BN_j\cong H\otimes_AN_j$, $(h\otimes b)\otimes x\mapsto h\otimes bx$, with inverse $h\otimes x\mapsto(h\otimes1)\otimes x$, identify its scalar extension with tensoring its underlying $A$-complex by $H$. Exactness of the underlying $A$-complex and of the $B$-complex is the same equality of kernels and images. Faithful flatness of $H$ therefore gives both directions of the required exactness equivalence.

source.place: 00HB (definition-flat), parts (2) and (4); tensor products of algebras, Section 00CV

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] to $B\to C$ and the specified prime $\mathfrak q$ to obtain a prime $Q\subset C$ with $Q\cap B=\mathfrak q$. Its contraction to $H$ contains $\mathfrak mH$: for $a\in\mathfrak m$, $\iota(a)\otimes1=1\otimes a\in Q$. This contraction is proper because $Q$ is prime; since $\mathfrak mH=\mathfrak n$ is maximal, it equals $\mathfrak n$.

Let $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. For $s\in S$, multiplication by $s$ on $A$ is injective because $A$ is a domain. Tensoring with the flat $A$-module $H$ preserves this injection by [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection], so multiplication by $\iota(s)$ on $H$ is injective. Thus $\iota(s)$ is a nonzerodivisor, and [lem-pc-minimal-prime-avoids-nonzerodivisor] gives $\iota(s)\notin\mathfrak p_i$ for every $i$. Consequently $A\to H/\mathfrak p_i$ is injective, and the formula $a/s\mapsto\overline{\iota(a)}/\overline{\iota(s)}$ defines a compatible map $K\to L_i:=\operatorname{Frac}(H/\mathfrak p_i)$.

source.place: 00HB (definition-flat), and minimal primes and nonzerodivisors as in 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring)

proof.text: The inclusion $B\hookrightarrow K$ induces an injective map $C\hookrightarrow H\otimes_AK$ by [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection]. Identify $H\otimes_AK$ with $S^{-1}H$ by $h\otimes(a/s)\mapsto\iota(a)h/s$; the inverse is $h/s\mapsto h\otimes(1/s)$. These maps respect the fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and the tensor balancing relation and are inverse on the displayed generators. Write $\alpha:C\hookrightarrow S^{-1}H$ for this injection.

For every $i$ let $T_i$ be the integral closure of $H/\mathfrak p_i$ in $L_i$, and put $U=\prod_{i=1}^rT_i$. The map $B\to L_i$ of Step 4 lands in $T_i$: a monic equation for $b\in B$ over $A$ becomes the same monic equation over $H/\mathfrak p_i$. Thus [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] and [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property] give a homomorphism $\psi_i:C\to T_i$, $h\otimes b\mapsto\bar h\,b_i$, where $b_i$ denotes the image of $b$ in $L_i$. Put $\psi=(\psi_i)_i:C\to U$ and $D=\psi(C)\subset U$. If $\alpha(c)=h/s$, its $i$-th component in $L_i$ is $\bar h/\overline{\iota(s)}$, by the formula of Step 5.

The kernel of $\psi$ consists of nilpotent elements. Indeed, if $\psi(c)=0$ and $\alpha(c)=h/s$, Step 4 shows the denominator is nonzero in every $H/\mathfrak p_i$, so $h\in\mathfrak p_i$ for all $i$. Every prime of $H$ contains a minimal prime by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]; hence $h$ belongs to every prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] with $I=0$, $h^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$. Thus $\alpha(c^N)=(h/s)^N=0$, and injectivity of $\alpha$ gives $c^N=0$. Since $Q$ is prime, $\ker\psi\subset Q$. Accordingly $P:=\psi(Q)$ is a proper prime ideal of $D$: for $\psi(x)\psi(y)\in P$, choose $z\in Q$ with $\psi(xy)=\psi(z)$; then $xy-z\in\ker\psi\subset Q$, so $x\in Q$ or $y\in Q$. Also $\psi^{-1}(P)=Q$.

The inclusion $D\hookrightarrow U$ is integral. For $t=(t_i)_i\in U$, choose a monic polynomial $f_i\in(H/\mathfrak p_i)[X]$ vanishing at $t_i$, by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Lift its coefficients to obtain a monic $F_i\in H[X]$. The finite product $F=\prod_iF_i$ is monic and annihilates $t$ in $U$, because its $i$-th coordinate has the vanishing factor $f_i(t_i)$. The image of $H$ in $U$ is contained in $D$ (it is $\psi(h\otimes1)$), so the same polynomial is a monic equation over $D$ for $t$.

source.place: 00GI (definition-integral) and 00GO (lemma-integral-closure-is-ring); finite product argument underlying the normalization decomposition

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] to $D\hookrightarrow U$ and $P$ to obtain a prime $M_U\subset U$ with $M_U\cap D=P$. Therefore $\psi^{-1}(M_U)=Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-product-prime-factor] there are an index $i$ and a prime $M\subset T_i$ with $M_U=\operatorname{pr}_i^{-1}(M)$. In particular the index set is nonempty; the empty-product case cannot support $M_U$.

Set $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_i$, $T=T_i$ and $j(b)=\psi_i(1\otimes b)$. Then $j^{-1}(M)=\mathfrak q$: explicitly, $j(b)\in M$ if and only if $\psi(1\otimes b)\in M_U$, if and only if $1\otimes b\in Q$, if and only if $b\in\mathfrak q$. Likewise the inverse image of $M$ in $H$ is the contraction $Q\cap H=\mathfrak n$ from Step 3. Since the map $H\to T_i$ factors through $H/\mathfrak p_i$, the inverse image in that quotient is exactly $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak p_i$. Finally $j(a)=\psi_i(1\otimes a)=\psi_i(\iota(a)\otimes1)$ for $a\in A$, which is precisely the required $A$-algebra compatibility. The prime $\mathfrak p_i$ is minimal by its choice in Step 1.

source.place: Conclusion from the tensor balancing relation and contraction identities proved in Steps 1, 3, 6 and 9
